equity.level_reason: Prisoners (incarceration, an SES component) get group-specific results (97% cure/completion, no defaults) described as better than civilians, but no disparity is framed and the civilian contrast is not quantified.

level_alternative.reason: Prisoners could be read as a program population subgroup rather than an SPD comparison; the explanation given is screening and adherence, not social position.

ev.q: Cure and completion rates among prisoners were high (97%), with no prison patients defaulting.

equity.equity_measurement: Prisoners (n=39) vs civilians (n=310); civilian treatment success is not given separately, so the contrast is described rather than quantified. The WHO 85% target is a general program target, not an equity target.

notes: The only test is the symptomatic vs screened culture-confirmation contrast (p<0.001). Treatment outcomes by quarter cohort and patient group are set side by side and judged against the WHO 85% target; comparisons with other Russian DOTS sites are cited from earlier reports.
view_issues: Text says success was higher among radiographically diagnosed patients without bacteriologic confirmation, but no figure for that group is reported.
